You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: H0834d

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "As, just as (comparative); when (temporal); because, since (causal); according to what; after"
  Readable gloss: "The compound conjunction ka'asher (literally 'as that which') is one of Hebrew's most versatile subordinators, built from the preposition ke ('as, like') and the relative particle asher. Its primary function is comparative — 'as God commanded Noah' (Gen 7:9) — but it readily slides into temporal territory ('when he had finished speaking,' Gen 18:33) and occasionally marks cause ('because they did not fear the LORD,' 2 Kgs 17:26). This functional range mirrors the well-known polysemy of 'as' in English and comme in French, both of which span comparison, time, and reason. Spanish distinguishes the senses more sharply: como for comparison, cuando for time, and porque for cause."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "as, just as (comparative)"
    Enriched: Comparative: 'as,' 'just as,' 'like' — the dominant sense at roughly 83% of occurrences, establishing correspondence between two situations. The formulaic ka'asher tsivvah ('as [the LORD] commanded') recurs throughout the Pentateuch (Gen 7:9, 7:16, Exod 39:1). French comme and German wie render this uniformly, while Korean cheoreom distinguishes it from temporal uses.
    Existing Spanish translations: como
  Sense 2: "when (temporal)"
    Enriched: Temporal: 'when,' 'at the time that' — introducing a time clause. Abram entered Egypt 'when' (ka'asher) he drew near (Gen 12:11), and the LORD departed 'when' he finished speaking (Gen 18:33). Spanish cuando and German als clearly mark this temporal reading, separating it from comparative como/wie.
    Existing Spanish translations: cuando, que
  Sense 3: "and as, and just as (coordinated comparative)"
    Enriched: Coordinated comparative: 'and as,' 'and just as' — the comparative sense preceded by the conjunction waw. Functionally identical to sense 1 but within coordinated clauses like 'and as you have dealt kindly' (Gen 26:29). French et-comme and German und-wie reflect the conjunction-plus-comparison structure.
    Existing Spanish translations: Como, Como-cuando, Y-como, [como], como, como-el-que, como-quien, y-como, y-si
  Sense 4: "and when (coordinated temporal)"
    Enriched: Coordinated temporal: 'and when' — the temporal sense preceded by waw. Only three occurrences, including 'and when Moses held up his hand' (Exod 17:11) and 'and when your servants ask' (Ezek 37:18). Spanish y-cuando and German und-als mark both the coordination and the temporality.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-cuando, y-cuando, ¿y-cuando
  Sense 5: "because, since (causal)"
    Enriched: Causal: 'because,' 'since,' 'inasmuch as' — providing the reason for the main clause. In Josh 6:22 and 2 Kgs 17:26, ka'asher introduces the ground for an action. Spanish porque and German weil unambiguously signal causation, confirming this as a distinct sense rather than a comparative reading.
    Existing Spanish translations: como, lo-que, porque
  Sense 6: "according to what (conformity)"
    Enriched: Conformity: 'according to what,' 'in accordance with' — expressing compliance with a standard or instruction. Jephthah's daughter says 'do to me according to what has gone out of your mouth' (Judg 11:36). Spanish conforme a lo que isolates this nuance of conformity from simple comparison.
    Existing Spanish translations: como, conforme-a-lo-que
  Sense 7: "after (temporal sequence)"
    Enriched: Temporal sequence: 'after' — marking that the main clause follows the subordinate event. Only one occurrence in Ps 51:1 (superscription: 'after he had gone in to Bathsheba'). Spanish cuando and German nach render the sequential meaning, distinguishing it from simultaneous temporal 'when.'
    Existing Spanish translations: cuando-
